task: Write one sentence of your own using the word torrid. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know torrid should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By two o'clock the plaza is torrid, and the whole town shutters itself until the light begins to slant.
Balmy is warmth as a gift — shirtsleeve evenings, windows open; it is the mildest air on this scale, nowhere near the punishing heat of torrid.
Sweltering goes further than balmy — heat you sweat through, heavy and airless; torrid claims the most: heat with violence in it, the kind that names the equator's whole belt of the globe.

Scorching is heat named for what it does — it burns whatever it touches: pavement, paint, the back of your neck. Torrid is heat named for its rank: extreme, punishing, the top of the scale, whether or not anything has burned yet.

Blistering measures heat on your own skin — sun that raises blisters, a handrail you cannot hold. Torrid measures the place itself: air so extremely hot it punishes everyone in it, the heat that named the equator's whole belt.
